work.title: Stories of Ancient Stones: A Living Tradition of Indigenous People (Mundas) in Jharkhand, India
work.scope: Munda megalithic living traditions in multiple rural Munda villages in Ranchi, Jharkhand; participant ages 18-70; 15 Munda participants reported by the article.

identity_verification.repository_precheck: No exact-title result returned by repository code search before insertion.
identity_verification.canonicalization_rule: DOI landing page, provider HTML/download manifestation, indexing records and citations are manifestations/records of one scholarly work and must not be counted as independent corroborating sources.

exact_locator_candidates.note: Qualitative ethnographic/participatory design; multiple Ranchi Munda villages; 15 Munda participants; participant observation, interviews, oral narratives; verbal consent, pseudonyms/confidentiality, express permission for sensitive cultural information.
Article-attributed findings on megalithic cultural/ritual roles and gender dimensions; requires publication-page concordance and proposition-level dependency classification before promotion.
Article-attributed findings on modernization/land pressures and resistance; mixed field evidence and cited literature must be separated before promotion.

rights_access_consent.participant_consent_reported_by_article: verbal consent; withdrawal rights; pseudonyms/confidentiality; sensitive cultural information shared only with express permission
rights_access_consent.cultural_governance: Do not expose participant-sensitive or culturally restricted material merely because provider full text is public.

evidence_promotion.reason: Provider HTML supplies unusually strong exact-locator candidates, but publication-page concordance, primary-vs-secondary dependency tagging, file-level reuse terms, and cultural/consent review remain required before controlled promotion.

quality_uncertainty: Do not generalize a 15-participant Ranchi sample to all Munda communities or all periods.
Distinguish direct participant/fieldwork evidence from claims attributed to prior literature.
Participant quotations and named roles require heightened consent/context handling even where published.
Provider HTML line locators are audit locators, not substitutes for final journal page locators.
